acceptance: Capability-aware native callbacks execute against the current Vm HostContext instead of a process-global service, so two VMs can have different grants and providers without cross-run leakage.
The stdlib exposes a deny-by-default env module with get/has operations; both require env.read and never fabricate a value when the capability or provider is absent.
A deterministic EnvironmentSource can be installed per VM for tests and embedding, while the CLI default remains denied for env.read unless an explicit host profile grants it.
Native/module metadata or AHS records the env.read capability so tooling and package manifests can audit the requirement before execution.
A package declaring env.read is only an upper bound: host/project policy may narrow it, and a runtime call still faults with AIPO_RT_CAPABILITY_DENIED when the effective grant is absent.
Positive and negative tests cover denied access, granted deterministic reads, missing names, per-VM isolation, package capability declarations and VM↔host policy narrowing.
The capability boundary is documented, no filesystem/network/process/crypto surface is added accidentally, and fmt/clippy/test/doc gates remain green.
